title: Combining Like Terms (Single Variable, Coefficients, Mixed Constants)
preview: Walk from 3x + 4x through multi-variable, fractional/decimal coefficients, the implied 1 in front of x, and the case where nothing combines. Enrichment checks equivalence.

body.goal: Students identify like terms reliably across coefficient sign, multiple variables, mixed constants, and the cases where a coefficient of 1 is implied or where nothing combines at all.
body.launch: Run the integer warm-up so the arithmetic is hot. Then start the slice. Don't lecture about 'like terms' first — let the slice show what is and isn't combinable.
body.prerequisiteLabel: Warm up with the integer arithmetic the slice will need.

prerequisiteSteps.teacherNote: Both negative. Magnitudes add, sign stays.

steps.teacherNote: Constant in the mix — doesn't combine with the x's.
Two variables — only the x's combine.
Both groups, mixed signs. Watch for negative coefficients on the move.
Diamond: fractional coefficients. Common denominator first. Kids who handle step 8 freeze here.
Decimal coefficients. The 0.5 is a constant — doesn't combine with x.
Diamond: x has an implied coefficient of 1. Many kids write '5' or '5x' here.
Diamond: nothing combines. Answer is unchanged. Surprises kids who expect every problem to simplify.

enrichmentSteps.problem: Are these the same? 3(x + 2) + x and 4x + 6
Are these the same? x + x + x and 3x
enrichmentSteps.teacherNote: Same idea — three implied 1's add to 3.

body.consolidation: Pull it together. 'On step 11, where did the 4x come from when there was just an x? On step 12, why didn't anything combine? On step 9, what made fractions different from step 8?' Pull out: x is 1x, like terms must match variable AND power, and the move is the same regardless of fraction/decimal/integer coefficients.
